rationale.conceptual: The paper's method is a custom analytical shortcut for surfactant partitioning in cloud droplet activation, combining Köhler theory, the Gibbs adsorption equation, and the Szyskowski surface tension model. Correctly implementing the derived cubic equation for the common-ion case, along with locating the critical point of the Köhler curve, requires genuine understanding of the physics and careful translation of non-trivial mathematical relationships into code. This is not a standard off-the-shelf method.

The steps use only standard Python libraries (NumPy, SciPy) and produce simple CSV/JSON outputs. There is no external data fetching or heavy orchestration, making the engineering straightforward.
